title: One Password Each
about: Why every account needs its own password, and how to remember them all.

cards.situation: Mia loves her new passphrase. So she uses it everywhere.

image.alt: Mia holds one cyan key labelled violet cactus harbour pepper. Lines run from the key to the padlocks on all three apps on her phone: Game Club, Email and Music.

cards.prompt: **Tap** each app to see how Mia signs in.

parts.job: Mia signs in with her one passphrase: violet cactus harbour pepper.
Mia signs in with the same passphrase: violet cactus harbour pepper.
Mia signs in with the same passphrase again: violet cactus harbour pepper.

cards.explanation: One passphrase opens all three of Mia's apps.

cards.prompt: Game Club leaks Mia's password. What can the scammer open?

image.alt: Mia's home screen: Game Club, Email and Music, all locked with the same cyan key. Game Club has a red Hacked! banner. Far away, the scammer holds a copy of the cyan key.
image.revealAlt: The scammer's copied key reaches all three apps, and Game Club, Email and Music all swing open.

cards.explanation: The scammer tries the stolen password everywhere, and Mia used it on all three apps.

cards.title: A leak
cards.body: When a site is hacked and passwords are stolen, that's a **leak**. Scammers try leaked passwords on other apps, so give every account its **own** password.

image.alt: Mia's home screen: Game Club has an amber key, Email a cyan key and Music a green key. Game Club's Hacked! banner is labelled leak. Caption: each has its own password.

cards.prompt: Mia gives each app its own password. Then Game Club leaks. **Tap** what the scammer can open now.

image.alt: Mia's home screen: Game Club has an amber key, Email a cyan key and Music a green key, all locked. Game Club has a red Hacked! banner. Far away, the scammer holds a copy of Game Club's amber key.
image.revealAlt: The amber key opens Game Club. It bounces off Email and Music, which stay locked.

cards.explanation: Right: the stolen key only fits Game Club, so Email and Music stay safe.
cards.nudge: Which app's key did the scammer copy?
cards.showAnswer: Only Game Club: each app has its own password, so one leak opens one app.

cards.prompt: Game Club leaks. Mia used that password everywhere. **Tap** the app to change first.

image.alt: Mia's home screen: Game Club, Email and Music all use the same cyan key, and Game Club has a red Hacked! banner. Below, Game Club's sign-in screen has a Forgot password? link: We'll email you a link.
image.revealAlt: Email gets a brand-new green key and locks again. Dotted lines show reset links going from Email to Game Club and Music: reset links come from Email, so Email gets a new key first.

cards.explanation: Yes: reset links go to your email, so whoever has it can reset the rest.
cards.nudge: Look at "Forgot password?": where does the reset link go?
cards.showAnswer: Email first: it can reset all your other passwords. Then give each app its own.

cards.prompt: You have 40 accounts. How can each have its own password? **Tap** the safest way.

image.alt: Your phone, full of apps, with a counter reading 40. Below, three choices: one key times 40; a sticky note reading game1, game2, game3; and a locked app holding many different keys.

options.text: An app that remembers each one

cards.explanation: That's a **password manager**: it remembers every password, so you only remember the one that opens it.
cards.nudge: If one of your 40 passwords leaks, what happens to the others?
cards.showAnswer: The app, called a **password manager**: one password for all 40, or a pattern that's quick to guess, lets one leak open the rest.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
Every account gets its own password; a **password manager** remembers them for you.

**Try this:** If your email password is used anywhere else, change it to a new passphrase. With a trusted adult, or on your own if you're 18+, set up a password manager.

**Next:** The second lock that stops a stolen password cold.
